the combination of SCD and Aβ pathology is a strong indicator of future cognitive decline in the elderly.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SCD, when coupled with the presence of amyloid, predicts the most rapid cognitive decline in the healthy elderly.
SCD, when combined with amyloid status, is the best predictor of cognitive decline in healthy, nondepressive elderly.
SCD and amyloid pathology interact to predict cognitive change, and this interaction may be mediated by working memory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SCD is a better predictor of future cognitive decline than depression in nondepressed elderly individuals.
SCD, as measured here, may be a useful clinical marker of cognitive decline in healthy, nondepressive elderly.
SCD, as a subjective experience of cognitive decline, may be a more sensitive measure than objective cognitive tests to detect early cognitive changes associated with Aβ pathology in healthy elderly.
